headline: A widened Saudi pipeline damage assessment and cancelled October cargoes to Europe wait out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX and $100.30 crude, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday - about ten hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources this hour and are unchanged: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range; VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range; WTI settled $100.30 (-1.58%) and Brent $103.87 (-0.91%). The Middle East supply file is the one thread that materially advanced. Reuters reporting from satellite imagery now places damage at three pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline rather than two, with full repair estimated at five to six weeks although partial pumping may resume sooner; the line normally moves 4-5 million barrels a day, roughly 4-5% of global supply. Aramco has told at least two European refining customers they will receive no crude in October, and buyers including Poland's Orlen are replacing those barrels with North Sea grades. Crude nonetheless fell on Friday, which is the important reading: the market is discounting this file commercially rather than chasing it, and Hormuz reroutes plus ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar are absorbing part of the loss. Friday itself was a quadruple-witching expiry alongside the quarterly Nasdaq-100 rebalance, in which SpaceX's index weighting more than doubled to roughly 2.82% from 1.28% and triggered an estimated $15.5-22 billion of programmatic buying at the close, with the new weighting effective Monday. That mechanical flow, not persistent momentum, is the better explanation for a close three points under the session high, and it is a reason not to read Friday as one-way structure. The week's policy anchor remains Wednesday's unanimous 12-0 FOMC hike lifting the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; the ten-year finished Friday near 5.006% and the H.15 two-year stood at 4.67% at the September 17 observation. Because a halted contract cannot produce shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding, Tail sits at its structural floor of 5 and rises only to 6 from 06:00Z Sunday as untested headline exposure accumulates toward a reopen that still falls outside this window. Stress drifts from 22 to 25 on evidence staleness rather than observed difficulty, and Confidence steps down from 76 to 63 for the same reason. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with no evidence-based danger window applicable. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell through 16, 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final thirteen hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive slots before ticking back to 22. Confidence held between 75 and 88, drifting lower only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode was mixed across the cash session, turned trend-up into the close, then normal for the whole post-settlement stretch.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about ten hours after the final slot here. Tail is held at 5 through Saturday and the Sunday small hours, lifting to 6 from 06:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen; that single point reflects proximity and accumulation, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 22 to 25, crossing into the moderate band late on staleness alone. Confidence steps down from 76 to 63, describing an evidence set ageing without refresh rather than rising danger. Dominant mode is normal throughout, because a closed market cannot express a trend. The conditional routes to a reopen gap are the widened Saudi East-West damage assessment and the cancelled October European allocations, the rates path after a hike that left the ten-year near 5%, and any weekend policy commentary. The Saudi Exchange Sunday session, roughly 07:00-12:00Z, is the only venue able to price the pipeline file before the window closes.
